newsitem.title: USA: Greenpeace vessel blocks ARCO oil rig.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace vessel blocks ARCO oil rig.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace said Wednesday it filed suit here against Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO) and placed a ship of protesters in Alaska to block an offshore drill from reaching an oil field.

As part of a stepped-up campaign to curb global warming, Greenpeace is protesting worldwide oil exploration and is currently staging a similar blockade against British Petroleum Co Plc's mobile oil platform in the North Atlantic.

At 1200 PDT/1700 GMT Wednesday, the group's vessel "MV Arctic Sunrise" blocked ARCO tugs from linking tow chains to the mobile rig. The rig, dubbed the "Death Star" by Greenpeace because of its 300 foot-squared concrete base, is moored about three miles off the northern Alaska coast.
ARCO hopes to move the rig 75 miles east this month to a drilling site where exploration is due to begin in November.
"We're not going to be able to move (the rig) unless the Arctic Sunrise moves," an ARCO spokesman in Alaska said.
Meanwhile, teams from the U.S. Coast Guard arrived around noon local Alaska time to establish a 500-yard "safety zone" around the rig.
A protester onboard Arctic Sunrise told Reuters by phone that his ship and the rig were in a standoff.
"We're going to wait to see what they do," said Greenpeace member Steve Sawyer. He said three smaller Greenpeace rafts were moored near the rig's towing chains.
In Los Angeles, a federal judge set a 1330 PDT/2030 GMT hearing to discuss Greenpeace's request for a temporary restaining order against the rig.

Greenpeace early Wednesday asked the court to halt the rig's journey, claiming ARCO had failed to obtain a permit to move it through Alaska waters. ARCO claims, that to the contrary, no permit is required.
